archetype.name: Play-In Team (offense holding, defense collapsing)
archetype.definition: A Golden State side coming off a losing year whose realistic band is the West's 8-10 range: an average-or-better offense that can win games, tied to a defense and frontcourt that currently can't hold them.

report.headline: 0-3 on the back of a broken defense, not a broken offense
report.take:
Golden State opens 0-3, 27th of 30 on the site, after a 37-45 season that already ended a run of four straight winning years. The record looks like a collapse, but the two halves of the team tell different stories. The offense is ordinary in a fine way: an ORtg of 112.6 ranks 13th, right around the league's 112.4. It is getting there by crashing the glass (ORB % of 35.4, 3rd), drawing fouls (FT Rate 33.1, 9th) and forcing turnovers that feed it extra chances (Opp TOV % 17.9, 3rd). That covers for poor shooting, an eFG % of 49.8 that ranks 23rd.

The defense is the whole problem. A DRtg of 124.0 ranks 29th, opponents are posting a 61.7% eFG %, the worst allowed in the league, and they are finishing at the rim at 78.5%, also worst and far above the league's 66.2. The defensive glass is just as bad: a DRB % of 65.1 (29th) means opponents are extending possessions in a way no Warriors team in this history has allowed. Last season's DRB % was 72.9 and the four years before that were higher. That points straight at the frontcourt, graded F. Draymond Green has a BPM of -8.2, Al Horford -7.8 with a 25.0 TS %, and Georges Niang -14.1 with a 33.4 TS % on a 21.2 USG %. The one big who popped, Charles Bassey, played 13 minutes in one game.

Three games is a tiny sample, and some of this will wash out. Opponents' rim percentage this far above the Warriors' own history (67.3 last year) is partly bad luck, and the losses were not all blowouts: 105-127 at the Lakers, but 108-111 to Memphis and 122-131 in Phoenix. The W vs Pt Diff of -1 says the margin earned about one win. The 44.7% share of points allowed to shooting guards is mostly the opponents' scorers, not a defensive hole: those players scored below their own averages. The roster numbers are noisy too. Stephen Curry has 47 points in two games on a 62.0 TS %, but with an On-Off of -23.0, while the bench guards Brandon Williams and Will Richard post big positive On-Off marks. Over 51-68 minutes, that is lineup noise more than a verdict.

Where this goes depends on whether the defense settles back toward last season's 115.6 DRtg, which would make this roughly the same fringe team again, or stays near its current level, which would make it a lottery team. The pace is slow (95.8 against a league 101.4), which limits possessions and tends to keep games close. The fix has to come from the frontcourt rotation, and nothing on this roster sheet says one is coming.

strengths.title: Extra possessions through effort stats
strengths.body: The offense lives on second chances and takeaways. The ORB % of 35.4 ranks 3rd and Opp TOV % of 17.9 ranks 3rd, and both are well above anything in this franchise's recent history. Offensive-rebounding rates tend to hold better than shooting, though some of this margin will shrink. It is the main reason an offense shooting poorly still rates as average.

strengths.title: Guards can still score
strengths.body: Curry has 47 points in two games on a 62.0 TS %, and De'Anthony Melton is at 75.4 TS % in 68 minutes. Brandon Williams is carrying a 34.2 USG % as the bench creator. Melton's efficiency will come down, but the backcourt has enough shot-making to keep the offense mid-pack. The catch is that Williams is listed Day-To-Day.

concerns.title: No resistance at the rim
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 78.5% within four feet, last in the league and far above the league's 66.2 and this team's 67.3 last season. Paired with the league's worst Opp eFG %, it explains most of the 29th-ranked defense. The rim number will regress because nothing is that extreme for long. Even so, the F frontcourt grade says the drop-off from the past is real, not just bad luck.

concerns.title: Losing the defensive glass
concerns.body: A DRB % of 65.1 ranks 29th and sits well below last season's 72.9, which was already the weakest in this five-year history. Every extra offensive rebound allowed undoes the turnovers the defense forces. With Denver and Minnesota next, two of the league's best rebounding teams, this gets tested immediately.

concerns.title: Frontcourt minutes are dead weight
concerns.body: Niang (BPM -14.1, 33.4 TS %), Green (-8.2) and Horford (-7.8, 25.0 TS %) are giving little at either end. Their combined Win Shares are below zero. Gui Santos, the minutes leader up front, is Day-To-Day, which could push even more time to the struggling options.

trend.note: Three losses, but the scoring rose each game, from 105 to 108 to 122. The defense swung from 111 allowed against Memphis to 131 in Phoenix, so the defense, not the offense, is what decides this team's nights.

weekAhead.headline: Five games, two road trips into elite teams, then a homestand
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with back-to-back road games at Denver and at Minnesota, the site's No. 1 team. Both punish exactly what Golden State does worst: Denver has an A+ frontcourt and is 2nd in rebounds per game, and Minnesota leads the league in DRB % and REB % with the best DRtg in the league. The Warriors' offensive-rebounding edge goes away against the Wolves, and their defensive-glass problem becomes a crisis against both.

The homestand is friendlier. The Lakers (3-0, 1st in ORtg) are a bad draw for a defense allowing the worst eFG % in the league. The Clippers, though, turn it over more than anyone, and the Warriors force turnovers at the 3rd-best rate. Phoenix is the softest matchup on the slate, with the league's worst DRtg and a defense giving up a league-high 55.5 points a game to point guards. A realistic week is one or two wins, most likely from the Clippers and Suns games at home.

keyMatchups.title: Glass war at Denver and Minnesota
keyMatchups.body: Golden State's 29th-ranked DRB % meets Denver (2nd in rebounds per game) and Minnesota (1st in REB %). If the Warriors can't finish defensive possessions, their forced turnovers stop mattering. This is the clearest test of whether the rebounding collapse is noise.

keyMatchups.title: Pressure on Clippers' ball security
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers turn it over at 20.2 TOV %, last in the league, and Golden State's defense forces turnovers at the 3rd-best rate. Live-ball steals are this team's easiest offense. That makes this its best chance at a win on the homestand.

keyMatchups.title: Curry against Phoenix's point guard leak
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix has the league's worst DRtg and lets point guards score a league-high 55.5 points a game, 20.5 over their own averages. Curry and Williams should feast. Phoenix also scored 131 on this defense last week, so it may still be a shootout.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the Warriors' DRB % climbs back toward the low 70s against Denver and Minnesota. If the defensive glass holds up, the defense can be fixed; if not, a slow start becomes a lost season.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the defense to improve from historically bad toward mediocre: opponents finishing 78.5% at the rim and a 65.1 DRB % are far outside anything in this franchise's recent history. Even a regressed version of this frontcourt, graded F, looks closer to last season's 115.6 DRtg than to the 2021-22 defense. The offense's rebounding and turnover edges should shrink, and its below-average shooting may not improve much. That points to roughly the same team as last year's 37-45, minus a few wins already lost and with a harder floor if the frontcourt doesn't stabilize.

I project 30 to 38 wins, with a DRtg settling between 114 and 118. The Play-In is reachable at the top of that range. The bottom of the range is a lottery team, which this start makes more likely than last year's result would suggest.
swingFactors: Frontcourt rotation finding a big who can rebound and defend the rim
Brandon Williams and Gui Santos returning from Day-To-Day

confidence.note: Three games; rim and rebounding rates this extreme are mostly noise this early.
